header.running_head: Rasulullaah ﷺ Refuses to Accept wealth given to him

blocks.text: Muslim then). When Hadhrat Hakeem (RA) went to sell it, Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed someone to purchase it for him. After buying it, Rasulullaah ﷺ put it on and entered the Masjid. Hadhrat Hakeem (RA) says, "I have never seen anyone look more outstanding in that clothing than Rasulullaah ﷺ. He was as striking as the full moon and when I saw him, I could not restrain myself from saying (these couplets which mean):

"How can rulers even think to issue commands after
the emergence of the clear, bright and gleaming one (Rasulullaah ﷺ because they are now all constrained to follow him)
When honour is matched to his, he surpasses them
Because honour has been poured over him like water poured over a person from a large bucket"
When he heard these couplets, Rasulullaah ﷺ smiled.[^1]

Hadhrat Hakeem bin Hizaam (RA) says that even during the Period of Ignorance, Rasulullaah ﷺ was the person he liked most. After Rasulullaah ﷺ announced his Nabuwaat and went to Madinah, Hadhrat Hakeem (RA) left (for Yemen) during the Hajj season. There he found a set of clothing that belonged to Dhu Yazan on sale for fifty Dirhams. He purchased it to give it as a gift to Rasulullaah ﷺ. When he brought it back (to Madinah), he did his best to make Rasulullaah ﷺ accept it, but Rasulullaah ﷺ refused. One of the narrators by the name of Ubaydullaah says that he thinks that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "We do not accept anything from the Mushrikeen. However, if you please, we could pay you for it." Hadhrat Hakeem (RA) then sold it to Rasulullaah ﷺ.

Narrating further, Hadhrat Hakeem (RA) says, "I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ wearing the clothes when he was on the pulpit. I have never seen anything as impressive as Rasulullaah ﷺ wearing those clothing that day." Rasulullaah ﷺ then gave the clothing to Usaama bin Zaid (RA) and when I once saw Usaama (RA) wearing it, I said, 'O Usaama! Are you wearing the clothes of Dhu Yazan?' Usaama replied, 'Yes! I am better than Dhu Yazan. My father is better than his father and my mother is better than his mother.' I then left for Makkah where the people were shocked to hear the statement of Usaama (RA)."[^2]
The Gift of a Horse and a Camel

Hadhrat Aamir bin Tufayl Aamiri (RA) reports that Aamir bin Maalik once gave Rasulullaah ﷺ a horse as a gift with a letter stating, "A sore has emerged on my stomach, so please send me the cure you have." Rasulullaah ﷺ refuse to accept the gift but sent to him a container of honey, telling him to use it as medication.
Another narration from Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) narrates that 'The Spear Juggler' (Aamir bin Maalik) once brought a gift for Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah
Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.177). Tabraani has also reported the narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.8 Pg.278). Haythami has commented on the chain of narrators.
Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.484), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.
